We need answer extract claims. Need follow schema. Review text: "This is a greAt adapter\nThis was a a good value and the charging power is quick and is a very durable item"

Need identify claims. Product adapter likely charger adapter. Claims:
- good value -> convenience_value / price_value positive evidence "good value"
- charging power is quick -> function_performance / charging_speed? "charging power is quick" maybe power_output or charging_speed. Quick charging indicates charging_speed. Evidence "charging power is quick". polarity positive.
- durable item -> reliability_durability / general_durability positive evidence "very durable item" maybe exact substring includes "is a very durable item". Need exact continuous substring. Could use "very durable item" but source says "is a very durable item". Exact continuous substring: "very durable item" is continuous. polarity positive.
Maybe title "This is a greAt adapter" is a claim? general product positive? Could be other? It says adapter, greAt. But "greAt" typo, positive general performance? Maybe not specific product claim? It asserts product quality? Could classify product_quality/material_build_quality? Hmm "This is a greAt adapter" general praise. Could be other_unknown/uncategorized? But taxonomy includes general_performance under function_performance. Adapter great could be general_performance positive. Evidence "greAt adapter". But we need not overextract? The instructions: extract product-review semantic claims. A review may contain zero/multiple. For every claim exactly one valid pair. "This is a greAt adapter" is a claim about adapter being great. Could be function_performance/general_performance positive. But maybe combined with title and body. We need decide.

We need output JSON only. Ensure valid pair: primary_topic from enum, secondary_topic from enum. Could include general_performance for great adapter. But "adapter" possibly product. I think include? It might be redundant with overall positive. But "great adapter" is semantic claim. Yet taxonomy "general_performance" under function_performance. Polarity positive. Evidence exact: "This is a greAt adapter" continuous. Hmm.

Review: "This was a a good value and the charging power is quick and is a very durable item". "a a" typo. Claims:
1 good value -> convenience_value/price_value positive, evidence "good value"
2 charging power is quick -> function_performance/charging_speed positive, evidence "charging power is quick"
3 very durable item -> reliability_durability/general_durability positive, evidence "very durable item" or "very durable item" exact. Note source has "is a very durable item"; "very durable item" continuous. Good.

Potential claim "adapter" "greAt adapter" -> general_performance. If include, maybe evidence "greAt adapter" or "This is a greAt adapter". But if we include title, does it overlap? Could be okay. But maybe expected only body claims. We need likely include title claim because title is part source_text. But "greAt" is weird capitalization. Evidence_span exact continuous substring: "greAt adapter" yes. Primary function_performance, secondary general_performance, polarity positive. But is "adapter" product category not a performance claim. "This is a great adapter" general quality. Could classify product_quality/material_build_quality? Hmm no, "great" general performance. The taxonomy has "general_performance" under function_performance, likely appropriate for overall function. But "great adapter" could be general_convenience? I'd choose function_performance/general_performance.

Need be careful: "charging power is quick" primary function_performance, secondary charging_speed or power_output? The wording "charging power is quick" semantically speed. If they said power is quick, that's charging_speed. Power output would be "powerful" or "fast charging"? But "charging power is quick" means charging speed. Could maybe power_output. Taxonomy secondary includes charging_speed and power_output. The claim "charging power is quick" is about speed, so charging_speed. Evidence "charging power is quick". Good.

"good value" under convenience_value/price_value. Good.

"very durable item" under reliability_durability/general_durability. Good.

Now ensure JSON schema: {"claims":[...]} with fields primary_topic etc. No extra. Use double quotes. Need no markdown? Likely final only JSON. Need exact evidence substrings from source_text. Source text contains newline. Evidence spans no newline except perhaps title. Use "This is a greAt adapter" exact. Source has that. Use "good value". Source: "This was a a good value and..." Contains "good value" yes. "charging power is quick" yes. "very durable item" yes. If we include title, evidence "This is a greAt adapter" exact.

Potential issue: "a a good value" weird; evidence "good value" okay. Polarity positive.

Maybe "charging power is quick" also product performance positive. Good.

Should we include "This was a a good value" as value? evidence "good value". Good.

Could there be "durable item" claim under reliability_durability/general_durability. yes.

Now decide final claims count. I'd include 4 claims. But maybe expected includes title. Is title considered part of review? source_text includes title. The task says SOURCE_TEXT. It includes title. So yes.

But beware "greAt" might not be exact? Source: "This is a greAt adapter" yes. Evidence exact substring "This is a greAt adapter". Good.

Need maybe not include title because it's not a product claim? It is product claim. "This is a greAt adapter" general. Fine.

Let's craft final JSON.

Use primary_topic exactly "function_performance", secondary "general_performance", polarity "positive", evidence_span "This is a greAt adapter". Then second etc. Order maybe as source: title, good value, charging power, durable. But "This is a greAt adapter" then "good value" etc.

Need ensure no additional properties. okay.

Final.

{"claims":[{"primary_topic":"function_performance","secondary_topic":"general_performance","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"This is a greAt adapter"},{"primary_topic":"convenience_value","secondary_topic":"price_value","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"good value"},{"primary_topic":"function_performance","secondary_topic":"charging_speed","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"charging power is quick"},{"primary_topic":"reliability_durability","secondary_topic":"general_durability","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"very durable item"}]}
